We employ unsupervised deep learning and anomaly detection methods to identify unusual patterns of variability in the light curves of 872,228 AGNs with known variability. We find that 8,504 light curves show anomalous behavior. Among these, 682 sources show evidence for two-state photometric behavior during the Gaia DR3 observing baseline. These 682 CSAGN candidates were selected using an automated statistical pattern recognition approach based on Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) to identify sources whose magnitude distributions are consistent with two preferred brightness levels, substantially reducing the need for human visual inspection in selecting the CSAGN candidates. The candidates tend to have fainter absolute magnitudes and lower redshifts than the non-anomalous Gaia variable AGN sample, suggesting that some may be accreting at lower rates. Our approach builds a large candidate sample with less reliance on human visual selection. Follow-up observations of these sources can help identify what drives changing-state transitions and clarify their connection to accretion-disk physics and supermassive black hole (SMBH) fueling.

title: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
summary: We develop a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), connecting microscopic dark-sector physics to nonlinear structure formation. We systematize particle-physics ingredients of representative SIDM models and map microscopic parameters and interactions onto structure-formation simulation inputs. These include internal-state populations and reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, inelastic and dissipative energy exchange, decay rates and recoil kinematics, and modifications to cosmological initial conditions. The numerical framework builds on the efficient, scalable SIDM infrastructure introduced in our companion work for the moving-mesh code AREPO-2, providing substantial performance gains over AREPO-1. We implement isotropic and anisotropic self-scattering with constant or velocity-dependent cross sections, multi-state and inelastic reactions, and dissipative scattering, complemented by a dedicated dark-matter decay module. For strongly forward-peaked interactions, the anisotropic hybrid SIDM scheme combines frequent small-angle drag-diffusion with explicit rare large-angle scattering, achieving speed-ups of up to $\sim100\times$ relative to fully anisotropic Monte Carlo in the tested configurations. We validate the implementations through beam-lattice deflection experiments, thermalization and uniform-box decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. These tests recover analytical predictions, establish consistency between equivalent numerical treatments, and reproduce published inelastic and dissipative SIDM benchmarks. The resulting modular framework connects dark-sector models to nonlinear astrophysical predictions, enabling exploration of microscopic interactions beyond standard isotropic, elastic SIDM.

title: Turning Selection Bias into a New Statistic: Asymmetry and Fringes of Lensed Gravitational Waves
summary: Gravitational waves (GWs) propagating across the Universe can be distorted by intervening lenses, producing characteristic wave-optics signatures. These effects are not incorporated into current matched-filtering searches and can therefore substantially reduce detection efficiency. The underlying mechanism is the signal-consistency test, which measures deviations between the observed and expected signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) distributions. We report a systematic study of the impact of gravitational lensing on signal-consistency tests, using a two-image interference model and representative signal-consistency statistics in both the time and frequency domains. We find that overlapping images produce sharply localized SNR residuals in the time domain, breaking the reflection symmetry of the autocorrelation about the merger time. Although interference fringes produce broadband SNR residuals in the frequency domain, both domains exhibit a minimum for high-mass signals when the fringe structure becomes comparable to the signal bandwidth. This highlights a limitation of current strategies that search for distorted lensed signals only among GW events detected by matched-filtering searches. Exploiting this asymmetry, we develop a statistic that separates selected down-ranked lensed injections from noise-background triggers and paired nonlensed injections, without extending the template bank. Our results establish the first connection between lensing observables and detection, paving the way for the discovery of lensed GWs.

title: Testing the 4-Point Correlation Function as a Probe of Parity Violation with the Quijote-Odd Simulations
summary: We investigate parity violation searches with the 4-Point Correlation Function (4PCF) using the Quijote and Quijote-Odd halo catalogs. Specifically, we explore the auto- and cross-correlation searching methodologies that have been previously used in the Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey (BOSS) and the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) searches. Although the Quijote-Odd simulations are initialized with a parity-violating primordial trispectrum, we find no statistically detectable parity-odd signal in the halo 4PCF. Instead, we find that the halo measurements are dominated by Poisson noise. We are able to distinguish this noise-dominated behavior from the response expected for a parity-odd signal. These results clarify how parity-sensitive 4PCF statistics respond to noise in a controlled simulation setting.

title: Establishing baseline model performances for optical turbulence forecasting
summary: Accurate forecasting of optical turbulence (OT) is useful to optimise telescope scheduling and maximising observing efficiency, as the performance of adaptive optics systems strongly depends on turbulence conditions. While various numerical weather prediction and machine learning models are developed to predict these complex turbulence properties, properly evaluating their added value requires well-defined baseline reference models. This study establishes baseline performance thresholds for key astroclimatic parameters using two distinct models: one forecasting the parameter average over a specific timescale, and the other forecasting the temporal evolution over the same specific timescale. We apply these frameworks to extensive, multi-year datasets from the sites of the Very Large Telescope (VLT) and the Large Binocular Telescope (LBT) and discuss the possibility of extrapolating reference values of forecast performances for other sites based on their optical turbulence statistical characteristics. Our results show that baseline predictive accuracy varies according to the observing site, the specific parameter, the chosen timescale, and the forecasting approach. Therefore, an OT forecasting model's accuracy cannot be quantified in absolute terms, but relatively to the baseline.

title: Anchoring the Chromospheric Activity$-$Rotation Relation: A Study of the Pleiades and Group X
summary: We present a study of the rotation and the chromospheric H$α$ activity of low-mass stars in the $\approx$120 Myr-old Pleiades and the $\approx$400 Myr-old Group X open clusters. We combine published and new rotation periods ($P_\mathrm{rot}$) from TESS and ZTF, and use LAMOST, SDSS, and MDM spectra to measure H$α$ equivalent widths (EWs). While overall the Group X distributions of $P_\mathrm{rot}$ and EWs are as expected, detailed comparisons to the Pleiades and to the 700-Myr-old benchmark Praesepe produce some surprises. For F through mid K stars, the Group X color$-$period sequence lies between those of the Pleiades and of Praesepe, as expected. But the $P_\mathrm{rot}$ for its late K and early M dwarfs and the Praesepe slow-rotator sequence overlap, indicating that the 700 Myr-old stars have not spun down significantly despite being nearly twice as old as their Group X counterparts. In the Rossby number$-L_\mathrm{Hα}/L_\mathrm{bol}$ plane, rapid rotators in Group X are saturated, as is seen in older clusters, whereas the rapid rotators in the Pleiades show a weak but measurable dependence of $L_\mathrm{Hα}/L_\mathrm{bol}$ on rotation. This implies that the chromospheric activity$-$rotation relation attains its mature form between 120 and 400 Myr. Dividing the sample by color reveals that K, M0, and M1 dwarfs are no longer saturated by $\approx$120 Myr, M2 and M3 dwarfs become unsaturated between $\approx$400 and $\approx$700 Myr, and later M dwarfs remain largely saturated through field ages even as their saturated $L_\mathrm{Hα}/L_\mathrm{bol}$ levels decline, indicating that chromospheric evolution is not determined by rotation period alone.

title: Mergers may not be the main channel for galaxy stellar mass growth at redshift $z\gtrsim5$: Predictions from cosmological hierarchical models and simulations
summary: Mergers are a crucial channel of galaxy growth, but their role relative to star formation remains uncertain at high redshift. Here we investigate merger rates and merger-driven stellar mass assembly for galaxies with stellar mass $M_\star \gtrsim 10^8 \, {\rm M_{\odot}}$ at $z\simeq 5-11$, by combining complementary theoretical approaches within $Λ$CDM. These include the DECODE semi-empirical model, the TNG100 and EAGLE hydrodynamical simulations, and the \textsc{L-Galaxies} semi-analytical model, together with the Millennium and TNG100-Dark simulations used to examine dark matter subhalo statistics and merger timescales. This compares models with different treatments of baryonic physics and galaxy-halo connections. We find that dark matter-only simulations predict merger timescales $\sim 30\%$ longer than those inferred from cosmological simulations including baryons. Galaxy major merger ($M_{\rm \star,sat} / M_{\rm \star,cen} > 0.25$) rates are high at cosmic dawn and increase towards earlier epochs, reaching $\sim 1/{\rm Gyr}$ at $z\sim 5$ and peaking at $\sim 3/{\rm Gyr}$ at $z\sim 8$. Despite these high rates, mergers contribute only $\lesssim 10\%$ of the total cosmic stellar mass density evolution. The ex-situ stellar mass fraction ranges from a few percent to $\sim 20\%$ for all galaxies at $z\gtrsim 5$, across different models and simulations. Their broad agreement implies that stellar mass assembly at cosmic dawn is dominated by in-situ star formation rather than mergers. These findings suggest that the high pair fractions identified by JWST may not directly trace efficient ex-situ stellar mass growth, highlighting the need for physically motivated merger timescales to interpret galaxy assembly in the early Universe.

title: CosmoForge II. An exact treatment of arbitrary linear filters in quadratic maximum-likelihood power spectrum estimation
summary: Ground-based cosmic microwave background (CMB) experiments filter their time-ordered data to remove $1/f$ noise and ground pickup, which removes or mixes the large angular scales where primordial $B$ modes peak. A common remedy is a pseudo-$C_\ell$ estimator with harmonic $B$-purification and a transfer function measured from simulations. Another applies it after a matrix-based $E/B$ purification of the maps. We extend the quadratic maximum-likelihood (QML) estimator of CosmoForge to filtered maps, treating the filter exactly: a linear filter conjugates the estimator's ingredients without altering its structure. The same holds for the pixel-based likelihood of CosmoForge, which gives the smallest error bar achievable on the same maps. We compare all methods in a simplified setup under several map-level filters through the error bars on bandpowers and on the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. QML sits $2$ to $4\%$ above the pixel-likelihood bound on $σ(r)$ in every filter state. At low noise, the pure pseudo-$C_\ell$ $σ(r)$ is $1.21$ times QML's without filtering, $3.0$ times under a scan filter along stripes of constant declination, and $3.7$ times under one from a toy constant-elevation scan. The matrix-purified pseudo-$C_\ell$ $σ(r)$ is at most $1.03$ times QML's except under the constant-elevation filters, where it reaches $1.10$. These factors shrink towards unity at higher noise. The pure pseudo-$C_\ell$ gap comes from apodisation and from harmonic $E/B$ separation; pixel-space separation closes it, except under the constant-elevation filters, which attenuate modes rather than remove them and widen the gap. QML stays within a few per cent of the optimal error bars without the tuning and simulated transfer functions of the pseudo-$C_\ell$ pipelines. Thus, CosmoForge provides a robust framework for power-spectrum estimation and inference on filtered maps. (Abridged)

title: IC 1297: The Most Distant Known X-ray Planetary Nebula and One of the Most Luminous
summary: We present the first targeted Einstein Probe (EP) X-ray observations of any planetary nebula (PN). Using the onboard Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT), we detect X-ray emission within the central region of IC 1297. The spectral analysis yields a plasma temperature of $kT = 0.086^{+0.054}_{-0.058}$ keV ($T\sim1.0 \times 10^{6}$ K), characteristic of shocked wind bubbles in PNe, whereas there is no evidence that its Wolf-Rayet central star emits X-rays. The absorption-corrected X-ray luminosity in the 0.3--2.0 keV energy band is $L_{\mathrm{X}} = 2.8 \times 10^{32}$ erg s$^{-1}$, also consistent with a hot bubble. At an adopted distance of $\sim3.8$ kpc, IC 1297 is the most distant X-ray emitting PN found to date, opening up a new observational window on hot-bubble formation and evolution. It is also among the most luminous known X-ray-emitting PNe. Our results demonstrate the capability of the EP FXT for detecting and characterizing faint, extended X-ray sources in the soft X-ray band for distant PNe, extending the known spectral properties of detectable X-ray emitting PNe. We also compiled the X-ray properties of all 41 known Galactic XPNe, finding a clear correlation between distance and X-ray luminosity that reflects an observational bias toward detecting the brightest sources at large distances. The compilation also shows a separation in X-ray luminosity between hot bubbles powered by H-rich and [WR]-type central stars, with the latter reaching luminosities up to an order of magnitude higher. The ten most luminous XPNe all host [WR]/PG 1159 central stars.

title: Non-equilibrium chemistry and radiation hydrodynamics in metal-poor and metal-rich interstellar gas
summary: We present a flexible implementation of non-equilibrium chemical networks with the $\texttt{KROME}$ framework, coupled to a nonlocal variable Eddington tensor-closed radiation transport scheme ($\texttt{VETTAM}$). Our fiducial network is designed to explicitly capture the formation pathways of important molecular species such as CO, OH, and $\rm H_2O$, intermediaries like $\rm H_3^+$, and the destruction of these species through photon and cosmic-ray dissociation. We validate our scheme through benchmark tests, and demonstrate its success in 1D and 3D problems covering a broad range of metallicities ($0 \leq Z \lesssim \rm Z_{\odot}$) and densities ($n \lesssim 10^{17} \, \rm cm^{-3}$). We confirm earlier works that suggest that OH and $\rm H_2O$ are the key molecular species in dense gas ($n \gtrsim 10^{5} \, \rm cm^{-3}$) for $Z\lesssim 0.01 \rm Z_{\odot}$, dominate the cooling at these densities, and demonstrate that our scheme can reproduce their abundances with similar accuracy as dedicated static photo-dissociation region (PDR) codes. We also find that the dominant fine-structure coolant in dense ($n \gtrsim 10^3 \, \, \rm cm^{-3}$) PDRs transitions from CI to CII to OI at increasingly lower $Z$. Finally, we find that in turbulent media, rapid mixing at PDR interfaces renders the chemical species out of equilibrium, and show that this could potentially alleviate the long-standing problem of (static) PDR models producing excess CI in the diffuse ISM over UV absorption-line measurements. We conclude by presenting and comparing with alternative implementations of reduced but faster chemical networks in our scheme, discussing the problem-dependent performance-accuracy tradeoffs and future prospects.

title: Charge Response Simulation of Liquid Argon Compton Cameras for Precise MeV Gamma-Ray Event Reconstruction
summary: We studied the detector response for a liquid-argon time-projection chamber (LArTPC) Compton camera targeting MeV gamma-ray astronomy by a Geant4-based Monte Carlo simulation. The simulation, implemented within ComptonSoft, incorporates electron-ion recombination, charge diffusion, and induction on the electrode pixels. We evaluated the angular resolution measure (ARM) and the energy reconstruction error as functions of electronic noise, pixel pitch, and the recombination correction method. An electronic noise level of 4 keV and a pixel pitch of 1 mm yield an ARM (FWHM) of about 3 degrees at 1332.5 keV and an energy reconstruction error better than 4\% for incident energies of 1173.2 keV and above. Recombination correction using both scintillation light and charge signals improves the ARM and the energy error by factors of 1.7--2.3 and 2.2--5.4, respectively, compared to the charge-only correction, although the uncertainty of the recombination-fluctuation model remains. Since this simulation relies on idealized assumptions such as the use of the Monte Carlo truth in the event reconstruction, these values represent the best cases achievable under these detector conditions; nevertheless, they show that a large-scale LArTPC is a promising Compton camera for cosmic MeV gamma-ray observations.

title: Validation of harmonic-space likelihood methods for LiteBIRD B-mode polarisation analysis
summary: The LiteBIRD satellite mission aims to measure the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ with unprecedented sensitivity through observations of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) $B$-mode polarisation. Robust constraints on $r$ require accurate likelihood modelling across a wide range of angular scales. In this work, we validate harmonic-space likelihood methods against pixel-based benchmarks using 20\,000 end-to-end simulations that include CMB, instrumental noise, and Galactic foreground residuals processed through a realistic component-separation pipeline. We compare a debiased pixel-based likelihood, which serves as our benchmark on large scales ($\ell\leq32$), with an offset Hamimeche \& Lewis (oHL) likelihood applicable across the full multipole range. We systematically explore the space of analysis settings, identifying the number of simulations used for covariance estimation and the choice of beam window function as the most critical factors. Over the full multipole range considered ($\ell\leq128$), where the benchmark combines the pixel-based likelihood at $\ell\leq32$ with a harmonic one at smaller scales, the 68\% upper bound on $r$ from the oHL likelihood is $19$--$29\%$ larger than the benchmark one, depending on the beam window function. This demonstrates its viability as a computationally efficient baseline for LiteBIRD data analysis and cosmological inference from the polarisation $B$-mode field.

title: An All-Sky Search for Moving Gamma-Ray Sources with Fermi-LAT
summary: Nearby compact gamma-ray sources can move appreciably during the Fermi-LAT mission and thus evade searches that assume a stationary sky. Compact dark matter halos, dark matter spikes around primordial black holes (PBH), and evaporating PBH provide potential examples. We perform a novel all-sky search for steady point sources moving at 0.25 deg/yr-0.8deg/yr in ten years of 1-100 GeV Fermi-LAT data. For a transverse speed of 200 km/s, this angular range probes distances of roughly $3.0\times10^3$ AU to $9.7\times10^3$ AU. We find 577 candidate tracks, consistent with $533\pm27.0$ tracks in time-scrambled skies. We place a model-independent 90% upper limit of 80.8 recovered signal tracks. At peak calibrated sensitivity, this corresponds to fewer than 123 steady, full-sky sources with an incident $E^{-2}$ photon spectrum. We give the calibrated detection efficiency of the search to steady point sources and use it to derive illustrative constraints on both evaporating PBHs and PBHs surrounded by annihilating dark matter halos.

title: TDCOSMO 2026: new insights on the Hubble tension from strong lensing time delays
summary: We discuss the measurement of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) in flat $Λ$ cold dark matter cosmology based on the blind hierarchical analysis of 11 multiply-imaged quasars (hereafter the TDCOSMO-2026 sample) and described in greater detail in a companion paper. In addition to the time delays, we use lens models based on high-resolution imaging from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), analyzed jointly with axisymmetric dynamical models based on JWST-NIRSpec, VLT-MUSE, and Keck-KCWI spectroscopy. Our primary result $H_0=71.1^{+2.4}_{-2.3}$ km.s$^{-1}$.Mpc$^{-1}$ is based on the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, in combination with $Ω_{\rm m}$ constraints from the DES-Dovekie supernova (SN) dataset. Our 3% precision accounts for the mass-sheet degeneracy. Importantly, our measurement is independent of the local distance ladder (LDL). Among individual late-universe probes, only the traditional LDL is more precise. We discuss our result in the context of the Hubble tension, the difference between $H_0$ measured in the late universe and the prediction based on early-universe probes such as the cosmic microwave background (CMB). We construct combinations of independent late-universe probes and show that the tension with the Planck CMB prediction is robust to excluding any one of the methods based on Type-Ia Supernovae, Cepheids, or the Tip of the Red Giant Branch. For example, we construct a 'no-SN' $H_0$ measurement, by replacing the DES-Dovekie constraint on $Ω_{\rm m}$ with that from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations, and then combining TDCOSMO-2026 with independent non-SN late-universe probes. This 'no-SN' late-universe probe is in 3.7$σ$ tension with Planck. Even after completely excluding the LDL, the tension with Planck persists at the 2.7$σ$ level.

title: Stellar discs and intermediate-mass black holes in galactic nuclei II. Fragmenting the disc and forming the S-stars in a live nuclear star cluster
summary: We present direct $N$-body simulations of a stellar disc around the supermassive black hole Sgr~A*, perturbed by an intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) and embedded in a live nuclear star cluster. A retrograde IMBH with $m_\bullet=2000\,M_\odot$, relative inclination $θ_\bullet=150^\circ$, and initial semi-major axis $a_\bullet=0.15$~pc breaks the disc into three disc-like components and an angular momentum filament. The stochastic torques of the cluster, together with the IMBH's inward migration, increase the angular separation between these substructures. By ${\sim}5$~Myr, their separations become comparable to those among the observed Galactic-centre young star structures. The innermost ($a\le0.04$~pc) disc stars evolve into an S-star-like population. Relaxation driven by the cluster disperses their orbital planes, excites their eccentricities and depletes the `zone of avoidance' within ${\sim}10$~Myr even without an IMBH. The IMBH further accelerates their orbital-plane reorientation. However, the most eccentric S-stars may require an additional formation channel, such as the Hills mechanism. The distinctive signatures of the IMBH are the well-separated disc components and the eccentricity excitation confined to the radial range swept by its orbit. Dynamical friction from the cluster reduces the orbital size of a $2000\,M_\odot$ IMBH initially at $0.15$~pc by more than a factor of two within $10$~Myr. Prograde IMBHs tend to align with the stellar disc, whereas a $2000\,M_\odot$ retrograde IMBH can anti-align with the radially overlapping disc stars. We also quantify how the IMBH affects the supply of stars to the loss cone and the rates of stellar tidal disruptions and binary separations.

title: Ultralight scalars and invisible gravitons
summary: Unless the tensor to scalar ratio is small enough, the non-adiabatic mode associated with the ultralight bosons may be dangerously comparable with the adiabatic spectrum of curvature inhomogeneities. We point out here that this statement depends on the timeline of the post-inflationary expansion rate. Provided the decelerated evolution is slower than radiation for a sufficiently long period, the relative weight of the non-adiabatic and adiabatic components does not conflict with the direct constraints coming from the large-scale observations. Conversely the presence of ultralight bosons excludes the presence of long stages expanding faster than radiation. The synthesis of the light nuclei and the spectrum of the relic gravitons at high frequencies set the relevant constraints on the duration of the decelerated stages, on the delayed dominance of radiation and on the mass range of the ultralight scalars.

title: Blackbody evolution and circumstellar medium properties of broad-lined H-rich superluminous supernovae
summary: Broad-lined H-rich superluminous supernovae (SLSNe II) tend to show signs of interaction, including a UV excess compared to a blackbody function. However, a quantitative analysis of the CSM configuration and the UV excess has so far not been performed for most of the literature sample. Additionally, SN 2023gpw showed signs of asymmetry in its peculiar blackbody and spectral evolution, raising the question of whether similar properties can be found in other SLSNe II. We aim to characterize the circumstellar environment of SLSNe II by searching for signs of asymmetry, quantifying the UV excess, and investigating any IR echoes produced by dust. Diversity among SLSNe II is also explored. We fit blackbody functions to the SEDs of SLSNe II to quantify the UV excess luminosity and its evolution. We use this to investigate mass-loss rates required to produce the excess through interaction. We also investigate the line profiles in SLSN II at late times and compare line velocities to the blackbody radius evolution. We examine public WISE IR images and place constraints on IR echoes. We find mass loss rates of $\sim10^{-4}$ to $\sim0.03\, \mathrm{M_\odot}$~yr$^{-1}$ when assuming all interaction luminosity emerges in the UV, i.e., conservative lower limits for the total mass loss rate. Radii calculated from line velocities in late-time spectra are mostly too large for a spherical interaction photosphere, only compatible with the blackbody radius evolution if the CSM is non-spherical with a low filling factor. This is in some cases supported by a mismatch between spectroscopic and blackbody expansion velocities. Considerable diversity is seen in the sample, probably as a result of different viewing angles and CSM masses. WISE images seem too shallow to observe IR echoes in SLSNe II beyond $z\sim0.1$, but in the nearest event, SN 2020jhm, a likely IR echo is detected, suggesting pre-existing dust.

title: Ultraviolet Reflected-Light Spectroscopy of Modern Earth Analogs with Starshade Observations
summary: Characterizing rocky, habitable zone planets in reflected light is a key science objective for future direct imaging missions, and the ultraviolet (UV) is uniquely suited for supporting the characterization of Earth-like atmospheres. The Hartley-Huggins ozone band at $0.25 ~μ\mathrm{m}$ remains detectable at low spectral resolution down to $0.1\%$ PAL $\mathrm{O}_2$, providing a sensitive proxy for oxygen-bearing chemistry even for Proterozoic-like atmospheres where the visible and near-infrared $\mathrm{O}_2$ features become inaccessible. This work uses an end-to-end framework for UV starshade spectroscopy of modern Earth analogs that integrates high-fidelity observation simulation, conservative post-processing, and Bayesian spectral retrieval to quantify ozone detection significance. The framework is applied across 108 simulated scenes spanning a range of planet phase angles, system inclinations, and exozodiacal dust densities. The results establish that robust ozone detection with UV-only, $R=7$ reflected light spectroscopy requires a photometric $\mathrm{SNR} \sim 30$. UV starshade observations with the Habitable Worlds Observatory achieve this threshold within 3-day integrations for solar-type systems at 10 parsecs with inclinations up to $60^\circ$ at favorable phases ($\leq 90^\circ$). Above this SNR threshold, ozone detections are robust to systematic bias from imperfect exozodi calibration within $\sim30\%$, and the median retrieved ozone abundance remains accurate to within one order of magnitude of the true value.

title: Untangling Similarities and Differences in Star Formation Histories Across Cosmological Simulations
summary: How galaxies assemble depends on processes ranging from small-scale baryonic physics to large-scale cosmological assembly, which are difficult to disentangle with observations alone. Using $\sim$63,000 simulated galaxies from seven cosmological simulations spanning hydrodynamical, semi-analytic, and semi-empirical models, we explore how specific star formation histories (sSFHs) vary across modelling assumptions. Using non-linear dimensionality reduction (UMAP), we find that sSFH shape variation organizes along a few smooth axes in a 2D embedding, broadly corresponding to (1) peak timing, (2) peak sharpness, and (3) subsequent quenching rate. We identify sSFH shapes that many simulations share ("common"), well described to first order by dark matter halo assembly, and a few tied to individual simulations ("unique"), which likely reflect subgrid and parametrization choices such as merger-triggered burst prescriptions. A notable exception is a common population of rapidly quenched galaxies found across most simulations, likely driven by e.g., active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback, that halo assembly alone cannot reproduce. The origin of the most distinctive unique shape, an Illustris-dominated history with an early peak and slow decline, remains unclear, but we test the effects of short-term variability. With a multi-objective auto-encoder neural network, we recover the simulation that a given sSFH is drawn from with $\sim$95\% out-of-sample accuracy; ablation tests indicate this information is embedded in long-timescale sSFH morphology rather than short-term variability. These results provide avenues for theoretical and observational follow-up connecting star formation histories to subgrid physical models.

title: An upper limit on Galactic OB+black hole binaries from SDSS-V
summary: Binaries composed of a luminous OB star and a black hole (BH) are a key evolutionary link between massive stellar binaries and merging compact-object binaries, but only a handful are known and their occurrence fraction remains poorly constrained. We use multi-epoch spectroscopy from the SDSS-V Milky Way Mapper to place a first rigorous empirical upper limit on the fraction of Galactic massive ($\geq 10\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$) OB stars with a close BH companion, $f_\mathrm{BH}$. Radial-velocity (RV) variability alone cannot distinguish BH companions from the far more numerous luminous binaries. We therefore combine the SDSS-V RV variability measurements of 3130 massive OB stars with high-resolution follow-up and literature information to identify luminous companions among the RV-variable subset. Forward-modelling the detectability of OB+BH systems using BH masses and orbital parameters from binary-evolution models, we find $f_\mathrm{BH} \lesssim 3\%$ at 95% credibility. This empirical upper limit approaches, but does not exclude, theoretical predictions for the OB+BH fraction. The constraint is primarily limited by the number of RV-variable systems that can be decisively classified, highlighting the importance of complete, high-quality follow-up for future searches.

title: The Cosmic Radio Dipole and Observer Effects in SKA all-sky surveys
summary: The Square Kilometre Array (SKA) will observe our Universe on the largest scales and so enable the study of fundamental assumptions in cosmology, such as cosmic homogeneity and isotropy. Observations over recent years have reaffirmed an unexpected challenge to the Cosmological Principle first seen in measurements of the cosmic radio dipole. This dipole anisotropy is thought to be caused by our local observer motion, however, it is observed to be about three times larger than predicted, with significances exceeding 5$σ$. The SKA is in a unique position to shed light on this anomaly by measuring this and other effects related to our observer motion. To quantify this, we forecast the capability of large-angle HI and continuum surveys of the SKA to constrain the kinematic matter dipole in galaxy number counts, the modulation of the matter power spectrum by a kinematic dipole, and kinematic spectral distortions of diffuse radio emission.

title: Indirect Dark Matter Detection in the Multi-Messenger Era: Experiments, Systematics, Anomalies, and Prospects for Discovery
summary:
Indirect searches for dark matter (DM) span gamma rays, charged cosmic rays, neutrinos, X-rays, radio emission, the cosmic microwave background (CMB), and the 21~cm signal, but reported constraints and anomalies vary in evidential strength. This critical review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature from January 2000 through October 2026 using a structured search strategy.
  We assess observations through a framework linking particle interactions and halo source terms to propagation or cosmological energy deposition, instrumental response, background modeling, and statistical inference. Fermi-LAT observations of dwarf spheroidal galaxies provide robust GeV-scale benchmarks for DM annihilation, whereas Galactic-center searches offer higher expected signals but depend more on foregrounds and halo profiles. Charged-cosmic-ray measurements are precise but limited by propagation and source uncertainties, while neutrino searches offer complementary sensitivity through solar capture, directional and flavor information, and high-mass annihilation or decay. Several widely discussed signals, including the 3.5~keV line, 511~keV emission, the Galactic-center GeV excess, charged-particle features, cluster radio excesses, and candidate gamma-ray lines remain inconclusive because of limited independent confirmation, uncertain target scaling, spectral degeneracies, or background-modeling limitations.
  Cosmological observations provide complementary constraints from CMB energy-injection limits and 21~cm measurements of the intergalactic medium. Artificial intelligence increasingly supports reconstruction and inference but requires rigorous calibration and domain-shift validation. The strongest case for DM discovery would require statistically consistent evidence across independent targets, instruments, or messengers, under common particle-physics parameters, and with well-characterized uncertainties.

title: Initial Performance Tests of MASTA for Wide-Field Narrowband Imaging
summary: Wide-field narrowband imaging provides an efficient approach for mapping low-surface-brightness line emission over large angular scales. We present initial performance tests of Multi-Application Survey Telescope Array (MASTA) for narrowband imaging. Using commissioning data obtained with the QHY461 and COSMOS-8K cameras, we characterize the basic reduction procedure, photometric calibration, image quality, and point-source detection limits. The measured surface-brightness and point-source detection limits become deeper with increasing exposure time, roughly following the expected background-limited scaling. Under the current observing and reduction conditions, the COSMOS-8K camera generally reaches deeper surface-brightness limits, particularly in the red filters, while QHY461 has smaller pixel size and provides better sampling of the telescope point spread function (PSF). As demonstrations, we perform continuum subtraction for the nearby galaxy M106 and the supernova remnant Cygnus Loop using adjacent narrowband filters and reveal the Hα and [O III] structures in M106 and filamentary structures in the Cygnus Loop. We further compare the MASTA surface brightness Hα map of M106 with an independent SITELLE measurement. After accounting for [N II] contamination and the wavelength-dependent response of the 6544 Å filter in the f /1.7 converging beam, the corrected median ratio is 0.973. These tests indicate that MASTA is a promising facility for wide-field narrowband imaging. Further improvements in calibration frames, including flux calibration, field-dependent bandpass characterization, and spatially varying PSF modeling and matching will be required for quantitative studies of diffuse ionized gas.

title: EDGE-INFERNO: The chemical signatures of assembly history in reionization fossils
summary: In galaxies, stellar populations represent a superposition of both in situ and accreted components, tracing internal chemical evolution as well as the histories of merged satellites. We investigate how assembly history shapes the chemical properties of present-day stellar populations in low-mass dwarf galaxies. We analyze a suite of EDGE-INFERNO star-by-star cosmological zoom-in simulations of galaxies with present-day halo mass $\sim1.4\times10^9\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$. We systematically vary galaxy growth while preserving the present-day halo mass, engineering our simulations to span a continuum of assembly histories. Early-forming systems form most of their stars in a single progenitor, with centrally concentrated star formation and a continuous enrichment history. In contrast, our late-forming systems assemble by accretion of multiple progenitors with their own stellar populations, resulting in fragmented star formation across several halos with independent chemical evolution tracks. These regimes produce qualitatively different chemical signatures: single-progenitor systems exhibit connected, well-defined trends in abundance space, while multi-progenitor systems show multiple, distinct stellar populations with limited overlap. We find that metallicity distribution functions provide initial constraints on assembly history for samples of at least $50$-$100$ member stars. Multi-element abundance analysis significantly improves the recovery of distinct components, although robust reconstruction still requires larger samples. Fully separating in situ and accreted populations likely requires kinematic information. Accreted stars can contribute substantially even at high metallicities in multi-progenitor systems, while external enrichment can cause accreted material to follow similar chemical trends as in situ stars, particularly in the single-progenitor regime.

title: Delving into the depths of NGC 3783 with XRISM VI. Evidence for a failed wind based on Fe xxv absorption line variability
summary: NGC 3783 exhibits a prominent Fe XXV absorption trough in the time-averaged XRISM/Resolve spectrum. To investigate its short-term variability, we present a time-resolved analysis of the Fe XXV absorption line during the continuous 10-day observation. We divided the resolved absorption profile into five fixed velocity intervals and measured their normalized equivalent widths in 19 time-resolved spectra. Three velocity intervals exhibit significant equivalent-width (EW) variability. Two velocity intervals respond differently to low- and high-flux states with less emission line contamination. The time-dependent photoionisation modelling is unable to reproduce the most significant observed EW variation ($3.5 \, σ$), possibly owing to uncertainties in the assumed initial equilibrium state, which prevent a precise density measurement. Instead, using photoionisation calculations and assuming the high-density limit, we derive approximate constraints on the ionisation parameters of the two relevant components. The low-velocity component (-320 to -680 km/s) shows a delayed inverse response, indicating a high ionisation parameter, while its relatively short lag timescale indicates a relatively high density and a distance upper limit of 0.05 pc. In contrast, the high-velocity component (-680 to -1040 km/s) manifests a positive response with a longer lag to the ionising continuum, implying a relatively low ionisation parameter. This component appears to be less dense, with an inferred distance upper limit of 0.25 pc. The low-velocity component is consistent with a failed wind, as its outflow velocity is below the local escape velocity, whereas the high-velocity component lies near the escape threshold. Together with the lower-ionisation failed wind detected in 2001, this supports a multiphase failed-wind scenario in the unobscured state of NGC~3783 over more than two decades.

title: Intrinsic Soft X-ray Emission from the Hot Circumgalactic Medium in IllustrisTNG
summary: We study the intrinsic 0.5--2~keV emission of the hot circumgalactic medium (CGM) in the IllustrisTNG simulation TNG100-2 at redshifts 0, 0.1, and 0.2. We calculate the emission of gas cells with $T \geq 10^6$~K in the spherical shell between $0.15R_{500}$ and $R_{500}$ and compare samples selected by their star-formation activity. X-ray luminosity increases with halo mass, although the class-dependent fits cover different mass intervals. Among galaxies with positive luminosity and star formation rate (SFR), the high-activity sample retains a positive association after a linear adjustment for halo mass. The residual association is weaker in the quiescent subset with positive luminosity and SFR. Within $10^{11.75}<M_{500}/M_\odot<10^{12.25}$, the high-activity sample has more centrally concentrated emission and a median luminosity about five times that of the quiescent sample. The two populations have similar median hot-gas masses despite their different X-ray luminosities and radial profiles. These differences are consistent with variations in the spatial distribution and thermodynamic state of the emitting gas, although the samples are not matched in halo mass. Our results suggest that soft X-ray emission probes the structure of the hot CGM as well as its gas content, offering a way to investigate how star formation and feedback shape gaseous halos.

title: Dark Matter Stability from residual flavour symmetries
summary: We propose a model-independent framework in which Dark Matter stability emerges naturally from residual discrete $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetries left unbroken by the spontaneous breaking of continuous flavour symmetries, both Abelian and non-Abelian. No ad hoc stabilizing symmetry is required, as Dark Matter stability is an inherent consequence of the underlying flavour dynamics. As an explicit example, we construct a prototype model based on a $\text{SU}(2)_\text{F} \otimes \text{U}(1)_\text{F}$ Froggatt-Nielsen symmetry, which successfully reproduces the observed charged lepton mass spectrum and the PMNS mixing matrix, while identifying the lightest sterile neutrino as a stable Dark Matter candidate. Furthermore, we study the Dark Matter phenomenology within our model in the freeze-in regime, including production channels mediated by higher-dimensional operators suppressed by the cutoff scale $Λ$. Our analysis shows that continuous flavour symmetries can provide a unified, self-consistent framework addressing both the flavour puzzle and the origin, stability, and production of Dark Matter.

title: Extinction by non-spherical particles with the Nanoparticle Transition Matrix Code: perspectives for interstellar medium and exoplanetary atmospheres
summary: The Transition Matrix formalism (T-matrix) offers an optimal solution to the problem of radiation scattering and absorption by particles characterized by a high degree of chemical and structural complexity. However, its application to particle models composed by large numbers of constituents has been classically limited by the substantial computational burden of the method. As a consequence, the investigation of light scattering and absorption processes, in cases where particle asymmetry and non-homogeneity play an important role, typically need to rely on simplifying assumptions which affect the correct interpretation of transmission spectra and extinction curves. This problem has a huge impact on many fields of scientific application. In particular, it has a critical role in astrophysics, because the ability to model highly non homogeneous particles is a fundamental requirement to understand the role of extinction in different phases of the interstellar medium (ISM), as well as to probe the physics of light transmission in planetary atmospheres within the Solar System and beyond. In this work we describe the application of a new implementation of the T-matrix formalism, based on the framework originally developed by Borghese, Denti & Saija and named Nano-particle Transition Matrix code, which leverages the power of modern hardware architectures to reduce the computational costs related to the solution of relevant particle models for the investigation of dust in the ISM and of hot-Jupyter class planets atmospheric aerosols. This new implementation of the T-matrix formalism can handle calculations of increasing complexity with a direct impact in the interpretation of the transmission spectra of transiting exoplanets produced by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and of those expected from the Atmospheric Remote-sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large survey (ARIEL).

title: From Sky to Science: Time Domain Astronomy with the ILMT Survey
summary: The PyLMT transient detection pipeline has been operational since November 2023 and has detected $\sim$10,000 transients and variable objects in ILMT images in near real time. The survey has enabled the discovery and characterisation of a range of bright and faint optical transients. The detected population spans a broad diversity of astrophysical phenomena, including supernovae, variable stars, active galactic nuclei (AGN) variability, and Solar System objects such as asteroids and comets. We provide a concise overview of the detection of a variety of transient and variable classes identified with the ILMT, emphasising the survey's potential contributions to a broad class of astrophysical sources. We highlight representative science cases, including supernovae, AGNs, variable stars, and asteroids, to demonstrate the scientific potential of the ILMT survey.

title: TDCOSMO 2026: A 3% measurement of the Hubble constant from strong lensing and stellar kinematics
summary: We present cosmological constraints from 11 strongly lensed quasars with measured time delays (hereafter, the TDCOSMO-2026 sample). In addition to expanding the sample, we improve many aspects of our blind analysis with respect to our 2025 analysis. Among other improvements, spatially resolved kinematics are available for nine systems, including six with JWST-NIRSpec, compared to one in 2025; for three lens models, JWST-NIRCam images now replace HST; axisymmetric dynamical modeling is applied directly to the spatially resolved data, instead of an axisymmetric correction factor applied to spherical models; and the line-of-sight convergence is now based on the Euclid Flagship simulations instead of the Millennium Simulation. Our baseline and primary result is based on the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, in combination with a prior on $Ω_{\rm m}$ from the DES-Dovekie supernova sample. In the flat $Λ$ cold dark matter ($Λ$CDM) cosmology, we find $H_0=71.1^{+2.4}_{-2.3}$ km.s$^{-1}$.Mpc$^{-1}$, a 3.3% uncertainty that accounts for the mass-sheet degeneracy. The SLACS and SL2S samples are in excellent agreement with the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, improving the precision on $H_0$ in flat $Λ$CDM to 3.0%. Using the DESI-DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) likelihood instead of DES-Dovekie yields fully consistent results. We also present constraints in the open $Λ$CDM, $w$CDM, $w_0w_a$CDM, and $w_φ$CDM cosmologies; the TDCOSMO $H_0$ inference is robust and consistent across all of them. The combination of the TDCOSMO+SLACS+SL2S likelihood with those from DESI-DR2 and DES-Dovekie disfavors $w=-1$ at the $2.3$-$2.5σ$ level in all three dark energy extensions that we tested. We find, e.g., $w_0=-0.88^{+0.04}_{-0.05}$ in $w_φ$CDM and $w_0 = -0.85^{+0.07}_{-0.06}$ in $w_0w_a$CDM, while $w_a = -0.48^{+0.46}_{-0.44}$ remains consistent with zero.

title: Multiphase Analysis of (U)LIRG Nuclear Activity (MAUNA). I. Spatially Resolved Optical Emission-Line Diagnostics
summary: We present resolved optical integral-field spectroscopy of the 32 luminous and ultraluminous infrared galaxy systems of the Multiphase Analysis of (U)LIRG Nuclear Activity (MAUNA) sample, drawn from the GOALS survey and selected to have JWST/MIRI medium-resolution spectrometer (MRS) observations. The data set combines new Keck/KCWI observations of 10 systems with archival VLT/MUSE cubes for 22 systems, covering H$β$ to [S II] at ~1 arcsecond spatial resolution (~0.9 kpc at the sample median distance). Using the optical [N II]/H$α$ BPT diagram, we find that composite and LINER-like excitation together account for most of the classified area (median fractions 0.44 and 0.26), while Seyfert-like gas covers a median fraction of 0.02 but carries a far larger proportion of the line luminosity where it is present. Both the projected size of the Seyfert-classified region, $R_{\rm Sy}=0.08$-$7.5$ kpc, and its [O III] luminosity increase with the bolometric AGN luminosity, with $R_{\rm Sy}\propto L_{\rm AGN,bol}^{0.54\pm0.18}$, as expected for gas photoionized at a constant ionization parameter. The scatter about the luminosity relation depends on dust opacity: the [O III] luminosity per unit AGN luminosity falls by $1.09\pm0.25$ dex per unit depth of the 9.7 $μ$m silicate absorption feature (Spearman $ρ=-0.60$, $p=0.001$). Optical excitation diagnostics therefore locate AGN-excited gas reliably but systematically underestimate the luminosity the AGN supplies to the host in the most obscured (U)LIRGs.

title: The NIVARIA-Local Group simulations: Unveiling the origin of rotation curve diversity in dwarf galaxies and its connection to galaxy morphology
summary: Dwarf galaxies exhibit a large diversity in rotation curve shapes, challenging galaxy formation models within the $Λ$CDM paradigm. We present NIVARIA-LG, a new suite of cosmological simulations studying dwarf galaxy evolution in realistic Local Group environments. This intermediate-resolution pilot lays the groundwork for the full-scale NIVARIA project. The simulations combine constrained Local Group initial conditions from HESTIA with the NIHAO galaxy formation model. The simulated galaxies reproduce observed stellar-to-halo mass relations, match the Baryonic Tully-Fisher relation, and capture the distribution of stellar effective radii, including compact and diffuse galaxies. We analyse the structural and kinematic properties of isolated dwarf galaxies with $10^7 \lesssim M_\star/M_\odot \lesssim 10^{10}$, focusing on rotation curve diversity. NIVARIA-LG naturally produces a broad range of rotation curve shapes, including slowly rising systems underrepresented in previous simulations and steep rotation curves. We find that rotation curve diversity is primarily associated with gas extent and inner dark matter structure: more extended gas and shallower inner density profiles correspond to more slowly rising curves, while stellar effective radius shows little independent association. Individual galaxies show that rotation curve shapes change rapidly as gas is redistributed during assembly. Recent accretion events are also associated with more slowly rising curves in the most massive dwarfs. Together, these results suggest that rotation curve diversity is linked to the baryonic cycle, which shapes the inner dark matter distribution. The Local Group environment and its filaments influence this evolution by regulating gas accretion and redistribution, producing the observed diversity in rotation curve shapes.

title: Phase Separation of HI in the Draco Nebula: CNM formation Triggered by Colliding WNM Flows
summary: We investigate the thermal phase structures and kinematics of atomic hydrogen (H I) gas in the Draco nebula to clarify how infalling H I evolves toward cold atomic and molecular clouds. Using the DHIGLS H I 21 cm data, we apply the Regularized Optimization for Hyper-Spectral Analysis (ROHSA) algorithm to decompose the emission into spatially coherent Gaussian components, and classify them as warm neutral medium (WNM), lukewarm neutral medium (LNM), and cold neutral medium (CNM). We identify two kinematically distinct WNM components: WNM1 near $-3$ km s$^{-1}$ and WNM2 near $-30$ km s$^{-1}$. The LNM forms a broad velocity bridge between two WNMs, whereas the CNM is concentrated within a narrower intermediate velocity range. CO emission is also confined to this interval and is associated with CNM-rich regions. The H I mass fractions are $\sim 41\%$, $\sim 23\%$, $\sim 17\%$, and $\sim 19\%$ for WNM1, WNM2, LNM, and CNM, respectively, with the LNM and CNM together accounting for $\sim 36\%$ of the total H I mass. No comparably independent WNM component is recovered at intermediate velocities, although a weak broad component may remain unresolved. The observed phase structures are consistent with a dynamically compressed multiphase interaction layer in which compression increases the gas density, shortens the radiative cooling time, and drives the evolution from WNM through thermally unstable gas toward the CNM. The present interaction may both create new CNM, and further compress or grow pre-existing dense structures. Our results provide the missing link between previous evidence for dynamical interaction and molecular cloud formation in Draco, and identify CNM formation as a key step in transforming gas accreting toward the Galactic disk into cold atomic and molecular clouds.

title: Elastic Properties of Titan Tholins Revealed by Brillouin Spectroscopy
summary: Titan tholins, complex organic solids synthesized by simulating photochemical processes in Titan's atmosphere, are widely regarded as analogs to organic surface materials on the Saturnian moon. Their mechanical properties are critical for understanding the evolution of Titan's geomorphology and crustal layering. Here, we report the first direct experimental determination of the complete set of aggregate elastic moduli of tholins using Brillouin spectroscopy. Measurements conducted on tholin powder samples yielded a bulk modulus of 11 (2) GPa and a shear modulus of 3.9 (5) GPa, from which we derive a Young's modulus of 11 (1) GPa and a Poisson's ratio of 0.34 (3). Thin-film samples synthesized under slightly different conditions yield similar results. Compared with other Titan-relevant organic compounds, tholins exhibit the highest elastic stiffness measured to date, exceeding even H2O ice in both bulk and shear moduli. These results support the interpretation that complex organics contribute significantly to the mechanical stability and transport behavior of Titan's equatorial dune sediments. Measurements following prolonged atmospheric exposure reveal persistent stiffening of tholins that remains after vacuum treatment, likely associated with minor chemical modification and physical reorganization, highlighting the importance of controlled sample handling for future laboratory investigations. This study also demonstrates the effectiveness of Brillouin spectroscopy as a non-destructive technique for characterizing planetary organic materials and provides new constraints relevant to future seismic and geophysical investigations by the Dragonfly mission.

title: Broadband non-thermal emission predictions based on 3D simulations of supernova explosions within active galactic nuclei jets
summary: Thermonuclear and core-collapse supernovae are statistically expected to happen within extragalactic jets, as these jets cross the inner regions of their host galaxies, and supernova ejecta-jet interactions can potentially lead to strong non-thermal activity. We model the non-thermal emission from a supernova interacting with a jet on kiloparsec scales, using detailed numerical simulations of the interaction. Using a post-processing method, we applied a non-thermal model of the acceleration and transport of electron and their synchrotron and inverse Compton emissions, simplified and tuned for flexibility and computational speed, to the results of a three-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics simulation of the ejecta of a supernova interacting with an extragalactic jet. For intermediate jet powers, radio, optical and X-ray fluxes from supernova ejecta-jet interactions may be detectable for distances < 100Mpc. The non-thermal luminosity budget and local conditions associated with these interactions could be enough to explain knots seen in kiloparsec scale jets at different energies. These conditions might also be suitable for the production of heavy ultra high-energy cosmic rays, but photon and neutrino generation from hadronic processes would be minor on kiloparsec scales. The leptonic gamma-ray fluxes are modest but might non-negligibly contribute in TeV for the nearest or more powerful jet sources.

title: Ushering in high angular resolution observatories in the far-infrared: The case for a double-Fourier interferometer
summary: A far-infrared (far-IR) interferometer from a space-based platform would bring about a transformational improvement in the spatial detail of astronomical observations that are inaccessible from ground-based observatories. This orders-of-magnitude improvement would significantly advance studies of newly formed and mature exoplanetary systems and their potential for supporting life, the earliest stages of star formation, and the evolution of galaxies up to the peak of the Universe's star formation activity and beyond. In this work, we discuss the potential for such an instrument and the science it enables in complement to current long-term plans of the global astronomical community and in preparation for the next generation of observatories. We also outline notable far-IR mission concepts, pathfinder instruments, and technology development platforms that have been studied and developed throughout the past few decades and briefly discuss key enabling technologies.

title: Constraints on the cosmic reheating history from PTA data
summary: The cosmic reheating is an important epoch in the very early Universe, and has significant impacts on the primordial black hole (PBH) abundance and the scalar-induced gravitational wave (SIGW) spectrum. The relevant energy scale and the constituents of cosmic medium are encoded in the reheating frequency $f_{\mathrm{reh}}$ and the equation of state parameter $w$. In this work, we perform a full parameter space Bayesian inference, using the NANOGrav 15-yr dataset to constrain the thermal history of reheating. Treating $f_{\mathrm{reh}}$ and $w$ as free parameters, we systematically investigate the Dirac $δ$, narrow and broad log-normal primordial power spectra. Current pulsar timing array data can effectively constrain the peak frequency of the SIGW spectrum as $f_{\rm p}\sim 10^{-7.6}$--$10^{-7.0}$ Hz, along with $f_{\rm reh}\sim 10^{-9.0}$--$10^{-8.3}$ Hz and $w\sim 0.19$--$0.79$ (the $68\%$ confidence level), when the power spectrum has a relatively narrow width $Δ\lesssim 1$. A broader power spectrum introduces a smoothing effect that obscures the characteristic frequency knee in the SIGW spectrum, leading to the loss of information about cosmic reheating. Furthermore, for the Dirac $δ$ and narrow spectra, the PBH masses associated with the SIGWs are anchored at the planetary mass scale around $10^{-6}$--$10^{-4} M_{\odot}$. This establishes a consistent physical framework that naturally bridges the nanohertz gravitational wave background with the dark matter candidates implied by the Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment microlensing events.

title: Radio ghosts: Radio polarimetry study of newly discovered cluster minihalo candidates or radio tailed galaxies
summary: Extended diffuse radio emission in the central regions of galaxy clusters is commonly associated with non-thermal processes in the intracluster medium (ICM), but its origin and the mechanisms responsible for sustaining it remain uncertain. We present the discovery and multi-wavelength analysis of two diffuse radio sources, MKTJ0355-4237 and MKTJ0355-4230, to assess their nature and investigate their radio spectral and magnetic field properties through radio polarimetric analysis. We use deep MeerKAT L-band (1.28 GHz) observations to perform spectral analysis of the diffuse emission and study its polarisation properties via rotation measure synthesis. These are complemented by eROSITA X-ray data and DESI photometric redshift catalogues to characterise the host cluster environments. MKTJ0355-4237 is confirmed as cluster-scale minihalo with extent of $\sim 400$ kpc, while the other diffuse source MKTJ0355-4230 remain uncertain and could be either associated with a radio minihalo or radio tailed galaxy. Both show steep spectra ($α\approx -0.7$ to $-0.8$) that steepen toward the outskirts ($α\lesssim -2.5$), consistent with spatial variations in electron ageing and re-acceleration. Polarised emission is detected in both systems, with fractional polarisation $\sim1\,\%$ in the centres and increasing in the outer regions of MKTJ0355-4237. MKTJ0355-4230 is associated with a previously uncatalogued cluster and shows an X-ray morphology offset from the brightest cluster galaxy, indicative of dynamical activity. MKTJ0355-4237 exhibits a sharply bounded internal radio deficit without a corresponding X-ray counterpart, within current sensitivity limits. The spectral steepening supports turbulent re-acceleration as the origin of the diffuse emission.

title: Simulating Ionospheric Distortions in Mock SKA-Low Solar Radio Observations
summary: The Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO) will provide unprecedented angular resolution for low-frequency solar radio imaging, enabling access to fine-scale coronal structures. However, the improved spatial resolution of SKA-Low also increases the sensitivity of solar images to ionospheric propagation effects. We investigate the impact of ionospheric fluctuations on simulated SKA-Low solar observations at 50, 100, 150, and 200 MHz using the \textsc{Karabo} simulator and turbulent, moving ionospheric phase screens. We quantify the resulting image distortions using spatial power spectral density (PSD) analysis and compare the SKA response with corresponding MWA simulations. The results show that ionospheric distortions are strongly scale- and frequency-dependent, with the maximum fractional PSD distortion decreasing with observing frequencies. SKA resolves ionospheric fluctuations over spatial scales that are largely smoothed by the MWA instrumental response, with significant distortions occurring on scales comparable to solar active-region structures. These results demonstrate that ionospheric propagation effects should be considered when interpreting high-resolution SKA-low solar radio images, particularly at the lower end of the frequency band.

title: Henrietta Leavitt's classical Cepheid relation
summary: The Leavitt & Pickering (1912) mean period-magnitude relation for SMC Cepheids exhibits correlated residuals relative to modern Gaia $B_G$ and Johnson $V$ photometry ($r_{δV/δL12}\approx0.76$). Therefore dispersion inherent to Leavitt's photographic photometry relation is not solely random scatter ($σ_{L12,B_G,V}=0.22\pm0.03,0.25\pm0.04,0.20\pm0^{m}.03$), and is potentially consistent with the partial encoding of combined effects from the elongated SMC, classical Cepheid instability strip, differential reddening, etc. OGLE data indicate that $\gtrsim870$ SMC variables identified by Leavitt (1908, Table 2) are classical Cepheids ($\gtrsim 90$ %), and the preliminary unphased Table 2 photometry likewise features correlated residuals relative to contemporary observations ($r_{δB_G/δL08-T2}\approx0.54$). Table 6 data in Leavitt (1908, $n=16$) define a highly linear Leavitt law over an extensive baseline ($r\approx-0.98$), but constitute a smaller sample than the later 1912 work ($n=25$).

title: Detectability of 21-cm Power Spectra from the Epoch of Reionization using Modern Radio Telescopes
summary: One of the unsolved questions in astrophysics and cosmology is the development of a robust physical model to explain the thermal history of the intergalactic medium during the epoch of reionization. Various astrophysical models have been proposed, but current models remain only partially constrained by available observations. To clarify this ambiguity, hydrodynamical, semi-numerical, and N-body simulations can help solve this issue. One notable simulation from the epoch of reionization is the 21SSD simulations, which provide high-resolution results for the global 21-cm brightness temperature and the 21-cm power spectrum during the epoch of reionization. The simulation includes 45 models spanning three key astrophysical parameters of X-ray emissivity, Lyman-band emissivity, and the X-ray hard-to-soft emissivity ratio. Distinct values of these parameters result in different models of this simulation. In this work, four active radio observatories, including HERA, MWA, GMRT, and LOFAR have been considered to investigate the sensitivity and thermal noise of the 21-cm power spectrum. Each observatory has a particular sensitivity based on its instrumental characteristics, which helps assess which models lie above the forecast sensitivity thresholds of current instruments.

title: WALLABY pilot survey: accurate and automated linewidth measurements from global HI profiles
summary: Current-generation 21-cm surveys of extragalactic neutral hydrogen (HI) with instruments such as FAST and ASKAP are providing detailed spectral and spatial information for over 10^5 galaxies. Future HI surveys with next-generation radio telescopes could provide sample sizes larger by orders of magnitude. There is therefore a need for accurate, automated, and reliable parameterisation of the HI emission from galaxies. We have developed an automated estimator for HI global profile widths to better enable studies of, for example, dynamical masses and Tully-Fisher distances. Our estimator is based on an implementation of the BusyFit profile-fitting algorithm, and converges for 95% of global profiles in the WALLABY pilot survey. Probability density functions are calculated for all profile parameters using Monte Carlo techniques, and example error parameterisations are given. We confirm that linewidth uncertainties depend primarily on the integrated signal-to-noise ratio, profile steepness, and the linewidth, consistent with previous studies. We compare several common linewidth definitions, and the width at 50% of the mean flux density (Wm50) is found to be the most robust measure of linewidth. We provide examples of the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation drawn from the WALLABY pilot survey.

title: The Simons Observatory: Frequency-resolved beam calibration for the SO SATs with POLOCALC
summary: We present a far-field beam calibration of the Simons Observatory (SO) Small Aperture Telescopes (SATs) using scanned single-frequency measurements of a drone-mounted source emitting in the 90 GHz band, where the SATs have an angular resolution of $\sim$30$'$. We then compare the results from two campaigns in April and December 2025 to the band-averaged beams from planet observations by the SATs. Measuring the telescope beam response at different frequencies across the observing bands enables modeling the system's frequency-dependent behavior. This helps track optical non-idealities. The comparison with planet beams informs the frequency resolution necessary to accurately reconstruct the band-averaged beams in this way; it uses only the average drone and planet products, as it is intended to demonstrate the feasibility of the frequency-resolved calibration scheme rather than to set the precise beam covariance and instrument requirements. We find that the beams of the two SATs near 90 GHz follow the frequency scaling expected for diffraction-limited optics, with only modest deviations observed in the nearest lobes of one telescope. We establish consistency between the real band-averaged planet beams and the synthesized drone band-averaged beams for the center wafers of both telescopes, with an average deviation smaller than 4% for multipoles $\ell < 500$.

title: The DAWN JWST Archive: A spectroscopically-informed population study of the physical properties of galaxies at z>2
summary: Charting the evolution of star-formation, stellar mass and dust build-up over cosmic time relies on the accurate characterisation of the stellar population properties of high redshift galaxies. We present a catalogue of spectroscopically derived physical properties for ~12,000 galaxies at z>2, with archival JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectroscopy and JWST/NIRCam imaging from the DAWN JWST Archive. We present a custom version of the SED fitting code BAGPIPES, used to perform joint spectrophotometric modelling of PRISM spectra and broadband NIRCam photometry. In doing so, we publicly release a science-ready catalogue of the physical properties of galaxies beyond cosmic noon. We report key physical properties, such as stellar masses, star-formation rates (SFR) and timescales, and V-band dust attenuation (Av). We further probe the recent star-formation histories (SFH) of galaxies via their SFRs on 3 Myr, 10 Myr, and 100 Myr timescales, capturing both rising and falling recent SFHs. Through dust-corrected ugi colour-colour diagrams of massive galaxies, we show how quiescent and dusty galaxies populate this colour space at z>2, with galaxies experiencing a recent downturn in star-formation occupying distinct parameter space. We also study the dustiest galaxies in our sample, showing that they are preferentially more massive and strongly star-forming relative to the parent sample, residing on the high-mass end of the star-forming main-sequence. The slope of the attenuation curve has a strong dependence on Av, varying from steep to shallow as the dust attenuation increases and the specific star-formation rate decreases. Our findings show that the unparalleled number statistics of this catalogue of spectroscopically derived stellar population properties uniquely enables the study star-formation, quenching and dust properties of galaxies from cosmic noon to cosmic dawn.

title: Searching for Nearby Supermassive Black Hole Binaries with GRAVITY
summary: We present a systematic interferometric search for close supermassive black hole (SMBH) binaries in 20 nearby type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGN) observed with VLTI/\grav. We investigate parsec-scale asymmetric emission by modeling the squared visibilities and closure phases with a single circular Gaussian component plus a background point source for the central AGN, and searching for additional compact companions through grid-based binary models. The robustness of the search is validated using injection-recovery simulations and point-spread-function diagnostics. Several features are identified in the initial significance maps, but only one candidate out of 20 shows a persistent compact asymmetry, corresponding to an observed incidence of $5\%$. If NGC~3783 is interpreted as a binary AGN, we derive a Poissonian one-sided $1σ$ upper limit of $f_{\rm bin}<16.5\%$ for GRAVITY-detectable binaries among bright nearby AGN (K<12.5) at separations of $\sim1$-$100$~pc. Conversely, if the observed asymmetry in NGC~3783 is associated with asymmetric circumnuclear dust emission, the corresponding upper limit on the binary fraction is $f_{\rm bin}<9.2\%$. We compare these results with predictions from the Horizon-AGN simulation, finding comparable binary fractions. We also noted that the expected fraction strongly depends on the assumed distribution of individual SMBH accretion rates within binaries, which is currently unresolved in cosmological models. Our results demonstrate the potential of infrared interferometry to identify parsec-scale binary AGN candidates and motivate future GRAVITY+ observations to expand the sample and follow up known candidates, helping to confirm their nature and distinguish genuine binaries from asymmetric nuclear structures.

title: A Spectroscopic Census of Cluster White Dwarfs from DESI, LAMOST, and SDSS
summary: Gaia has substantially expanded the sample of candidate white dwarfs (WDs) in open clusters, but many remain without spectroscopic characterization. We leverage the increasingly extensive archives of large public spectroscopic surveys to identify 62 candidate cluster WDs with available spectra from DESI, LAMOST, and SDSS. After discarding sources with very low S/N and unreliable host clusters, 44 candidates remain, including 37 non-magnetic DA WDs, of which 15 had not previously been characterized in the literature for cluster studies. We find that nine are consistent with single-star origins in their proposed host clusters, increasing the combined cluster DA initial--final mass relation (IFMR) sample to 132 WDs. All lie within $2σ$ of the best-fit IFMR from the most comprehensive recent cluster WD sample, suggesting these additions do not require recalibrating the empirical IFMR. One is a likely Hyades tidal-tail WD, providing further evidence that dynamical dispersal helps explain the long-standing WD deficit in the nearest cluster. We further compare WDs with spectra from multiple surveys. Among seven Praesepe WDs observed by both DESI and SDSS, DESI gives higher WD masses in six cases, with a mean difference of $0.067\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$, while the inferred progenitor masses differ by as much as $0.459\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. More broadly, nine of ten single-star cluster DAs with DESI spectra lie above the empirical IFMR, with a mean final-mass residual of $0.06\pm0.04\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. These results show that survey-dependent differences can strongly affect cluster WD parameters, and should be considered when combining heterogeneous spectroscopy in empirical IFMR studies.

title: Nonequilibrium framework for first-order phase transitions
summary: The first-order phase transition is central to electroweak baryogenesis and gravitational wave generation, yet thermal equilibrium effective potential analyses cannot describe the real-time non-equilibrium dynamics of the phase transition process. We use the Schwinger-Keldysh closed-time-path formalism of real-time finite-temperature field theory to study these effects. For the $φ^6$ model, we derive the effective action and the corresponding Langevin equation. We further extend the formalism to the two scalar fields case, obtaining the coupled Langevin equations. These results provide a theoretical framework for the bubble nucleation simulation of the non-equilibrium phase transition process, laying the foundation for reliable predictions of baryogenesis and gravitational wave signals.

title: Intermittency in the Multiphase ISM --- I. Extreme Density, Velocity, and Magnetic Fluctuations
summary: Intermittency is a fundamental property of astrophysical turbulence because it concentrates strong gradients, dissipation, and transport into rare, localized structures. In the multiphase interstellar medium (ISM), turbulent driving is especially important because the balance between compressive and solenoidal motions can regulate how extreme fluctuations are distributed among thermal phases. Yet conventional increment statistics quantify intermittency without identifying the structures that host it. We analyze three matched ideal-MHD simulations of a thermally multiphase neutral medium that differ only in the compressive fraction of the driving. Density, velocity, and magnetic-field increments are non-Gaussian in every thermal phase. Increasing compressive driving redistributes density and magnetic fluctuations preferentially into the cold gas rather than uniformly enhancing them across phases. We identify the structures associated with extreme increments using local, scale-matched diagnostics of compression, thermal gradients, vorticity, strain, magnetic curl, and magnetic tension. Extreme magnetic increments preferentially occur where magnetic curl and magnetic tension are simultaneously enhanced, more strongly than extreme velocity increments are associated with their kinematic hosts. Extreme velocity increments show comparable enrichment in vorticity and strain, whereas extreme density increments preferentially trace converging flows and thermal gradients only in the unstable medium. These associations weaken beyond a phase-dependent coherence scale. Our results show that turbulent driving controls how intermittency is partitioned among thermal phases, while distinct physical structures host extreme density, velocity, and magnetic fluctuations.

title: Graph Learning with Multiplicative Aggregation for Solar Filament Fragment Association Modeling in Full-disk H$α$ Images
summary: Solar filaments are prominent features in H$α$ observations. During their evolution, they often exhibit complex morphological and topological changes, which, due to line-of-sight projection effects, appear as fragmentation and merging. These phenomena make it difficult to reliably track solar filaments using automated methods, as the same structure may appear different over time. To address this issue, we formulate filament fragment association as a graph-based learning problem, where individual fragments are represented as nodes and candidate pairwise relationships are modeled as edges to infer whether fragments belong to the same filament. Furthermore, we propose a novel graph neural network (GNN) that incorporates multiplicative aggregation layers to enhance feature aggregation in the graph, replacing conventional additive aggregation with a multiplicative mechanism to better capture information between fragments. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves reliable performance in filament fragment association, validating the effectiveness of the graph-based formulation and the proposed multiplicative aggregation mechanism.

title: MeV dark matter decay forecasts for the COSI mission
summary: The decay of dark matter (DM) is a generic prediction of many particle physics models, producing distinctive monochromatic signatures in environments such as the Galactic halo. Searches for decaying DM in the elusive 'MeV gap' have remained conspicuously under-explored, despite well-motivated models including axion-like particles, sterile neutrinos, and hidden-sector scenarios predicting signatures in this energy range. The upcoming Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI) telescope will help bridge this gap. Designed to probe this energy band with high spectral resolution, low background, and wide field of view, COSI is well-suited for DM line searches at the MeV scale. In this work, we make projections for COSI's 2-year sensitivity for DM decay in the Milky Way halo using dedicated all-sky simulations incorporating COSI's predicted instrument response. We conclude that COSI will improve the sensitivity to the DM lifetime by more than an order of magnitude over the DM mass range 0.4 to 10 MeV.

title: Sulphur-bearing molecule survey towards prestellar and starless cores in the Perseus molecular cloud
